title: FHIR IG tooling: FHIR packages, Maven repository and SUSHI for the AST refresh
location: fhir-ig-tooling-v1-<ast-export-ref>-<hash>, in the calling IG repository's Actions cache
derivedInputs: the IG's sushi-config.yaml (its FHIR package dependencies) and ig.ini, and the AST exporter ref; NOT the Java (17), Node (20) or SUSHI versions, see notes
producer: ig-ast-refresh.yml, only on a run that rebuilds the AST
consumers: the same workflow's rebuild: SUSHI and the IG Publisher with the AST exporter

refresh.how: a missed key saves a new entry from what that run downloaded; restore-keys fall back to the newest entry with the same exporter ref, then any

savePolicy: any run that rebuilds and misses the key
verify: none: what is restored is used as found. FHIR packages are versioned by name, so a wrong one is a new download, but the SUSHI in ~/.npm-global is never re-checked (see notes)
uses: .github/workflows/ig-ast-refresh.yml:222 SUSHI install, skipped when a cached SUSHI is on PATH
notes: Recorded gap (CI speed 14's inventory): the key leaves out the toolchain. Java 17 and Node 20 are fixed in the workflow (setup-java, setup-node), so they move only with a workflow edit, which does not change the key. SUSHI is installed unpinned (`npm install -g fsh-sushi`) and only when none is on PATH, so a restored entry freezes whichever SUSHI version first filled it, and the restore-keys fallback carries it across key changes. Fix: pin SUSHI's version in the workflow (or the lock) and put Java, Node and SUSHI versions in the key; until then this cache's trust class stays unclassified.
